title: ZeroHour — AI Productivity Companion
description: 🚨 ZeroHour — AI-powered last-minute productivity companion | Built for Hackathon By CodingNinjas × Google (Vibe2Ship)
longDescription:
When you're about to miss a deadline, you don't need a reminder — you need a plan.

ZeroHour is a full-stack multi-agent AI system that actively plans, prioritizes, schedules, and nudges users before deadlines are missed. The hero feature, Panic Mode, lets users describe a crisis in natural language and receive a complete AI-generated action plan pushed directly to Google Calendar.

🤖 4-Agent AI Pipeline:
• Planner Agent — Gemini 2.5 Flash decomposes goals into time-boxed subtasks
• Prioritizer Agent — Ranks by urgency × impact (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
• Scheduler Agent — Creates real Google Calendar events via Calendar API v3
• Nudge Agent — Spring @Scheduled cron sends proactive email + in-app alerts at 24h, 6h, 1h

🛠 Tech Stack:
Backend: Java 17 + Spring Boot 3.x | Spring Security OAuth2 | AES-256 encryption
Frontend: React 18 + Vite + Tailwind CSS | Framer Motion | Server-Sent Events (SSE)
AI: Gemini 2.5 Flash (Google AI Studio)
Data: Firebase Firestore | Google OAuth 2.0
Infra: Docker (multi-stage) | Firebase Hosting | Google Cloud Run

🔗 Google Technologies: Gemini 2.5 Flash · AI Studio · OAuth 2.0 · Calendar API v3 · Gmail API · Firebase Firestore · Cloud Run (7 total)

✅ Features: Multi-turn conversational Panic Mode · Live agent thinking panel (SSE) · Real-time task dashboard · Proactive nudge system · Google Calendar auto-scheduling · Notification center · Settings with preference persistence

Live: zerohour-a84d3.web.app | GitHub: github.com/PG300604/ZeroHour

title: SkillShare
longDescription:
A full-stack web application that connects users with nearby collaborators based on shared skills — think Tinder, but for learning and building together.
Backend: Built with Spring Boot (Java 17) and secured using OAuth2 JWT authentication via Supabase as the identity provider. Designed a geolocation-based matching engine using the Haversine formula with dynamic radius expansion — starting at a 10km search radius and progressively expanding to 100km — ranking results by skill proficiency scores.
Database: Spring Data JPA + Hibernate with PostgreSQL in production and H2 for local development. Schema managed via JPA DDL auto with seed data via SQL scripts.
Frontend: React (Vite) with a swipe-card UI, real-time messaging, match overlays, and profile setup flows. Integrated Supabase for auth token management.
DevOps: Containerized the Spring Boot backend using a multi-stage Docker build (Maven build stage + lightweight JRE runtime stage). Frontend deployed on Vercel with CORS configured for cross-origin API calls.
🔧 Stack: Java · Spring Boot · Spring Security · OAuth2 · Hibernate/JPA · PostgreSQL · Docker · React · Maven · Supabase
